It is defined as the detrimental effects of exposure to (excessive) amounts of toxic lipid species, leading to increased mitochondrial β-oxidation, oxidative stress (OxS), and organellar dysfunction. Inhibitory effect of carvedilol on bedaquiline metabolism  Bedaquiline has recently been approved for the treatment of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. Carvedilol is a cardiovascular medication extensively used in the treatment of heart failure and hypertension. In this study, Sprague-Dawley rats, rat liver microsomes (RLM), human liver microsomes (HLM), and recombinant human CYP3A4 were used to explore the effect of carvedilol on the metabolism of bedaquiline.
